page: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. Built on the ARM64 architecture, this server features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz, with one thread per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 34 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with top-tier rankings in memory bandwidth, software compilation, and database operations. The instance achieves top-tier performance in Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and single-threaded and multi-threaded compression tasks. However, single-core CPU performance and LLM inference speeds for small and medium models fall into the average category.

The c9g.16xlarge offers high compute density and memory bandwidth efficiency relative to its hardware class, making it a cost-effective option for parallelized workloads that do not require x86 compatibility. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, meaning all storage must be network-attached and graphics-accelerated tasks are unsupported. Additionally, the 2.0 GB of memory per core limits its suitability for memory-intensive datasets.

This server is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, high-throughput web serving, database operations, and parallel data processing tasks. It is also well-suited for Redis deployments and distributed caching layers that benefit from high memory bandwidth.
